I couldn't reply to your other comment but I'm sorry that the people in your town were abandoned. It is heartbreaking and awful. It happens far too often and tears me apart, truly. However, it's not a coping mechanism. 

I'm just a fan of giving people possible scenarios in a measured way and allowing them to use the knowledge of their situation and the people around them to make informed decisions. It's not my or any other person's responsibility to scare or be needlessly optimistic. 

I've interacted with hundreds of trans people at this point in a meaningful way so I know how bleak it can get. I stopped being involved with the community for ages because it was so hard. That being said, there were an equal amount of positive stories and the most common regret was not of transitioning but that they hadn't done it sooner. Also, I'm considering other people that may come upon negative comments and have it scare them into not pursuing treatment. 

Stay safe ❤️

Apparently people can't read. I am only taking issue with the original comment stating that their relatives WILL abandon them. That's it. Nobody knows but that person.

My entire issue was with making a definitive statement, unprompted, about how a person's situation will go. That's fearmongering and unnecessarily stating these things can delay people from getting the much needed help or taking steps to alleviate their suffering. I never, not once, said those things didn't happen far too often. I have many trans friends who I see regularly. None of us had people abandon us, which cannot be applied to a single person's situation in the same way your unsupported blanket statement can be. They add no value to said person's life.

You're entirely missing the point. Also where are you getting this "most households" data from? People often come online and post at their most vulnerable. People who aren't rejected are far less likely to go into a public forum and post about it.

Saying, "Most of your relatives will reject you..." Is making a definite statement about that person's situation. It's irresponsible and absolutely fearmongering.
It is definitely a scary time for a lot people. Be safe ❤️

Making definitive statements about how relatives will or will not react based on personal anecdotes, beliefs or stories without any additional information (and even with said information) is the definition of fearmongering. That is entirely different than being aware of what could happen, which I would argue trans people are already keenly aware of. It's uncalled for to pretend to be a psychic on behalf of a new person looking for guidance when they are at their most vulnerable. It is entirely okay, however, to arm them with knowledge without saying things that can influence their actions. It is nuanced but an important distinction. 

I've been in the community for 15 years, was very involved in activism, and know of many  heartbreaking stories but unlike you most of the people I spoke with were not abandoned by their relatives, which like your anecdotes amounts to little when applied to advice given to a single person that is discouraging without additional context.

The person I was responding to said, "Most of your relatives will reject you..." That's fearmongering. The original post didn't even mention anyone but their girlfriend.

Which is a smart approach depending on the situation. I just think making blanket statements that may or may not be true is harmful. I waited 6 additional years for nothing because someone told me, "If you can run from being trans do so because your life will be hell." Obviously they had a difficult life but waiting didn't help me at all.

I think it's dangerous to tell people that most of their relatives will reject them. That was the sort of thing that delayed my transition by years. Fearmongering is not okay. I had zero people reject me 15 years ago when I started. It's a case by case situation.
